compute.reported_as: Appendix C: We note that the training of our ansatz was performed using P100 GPUs. In order to produce the results of Fig. 3(b), we use d_h = 300 and N_s = 100 samples for training. We have first performed annealing on the system size 6 x 6 with N_warmup = 1000, N_annealing = 10000, and an initial pseudo-temperature T_0 = 0.25, while using a fixed learning rate eta = 5 x 10^-4. During each annealing step, we perform N_train = 5 gradient descent steps. In this initial phase, we only apply the U(1) symmetry. In the next phase, we perform an additional 25000 gradients steps at zero pseudo-temperature and add an additional 25000 gradients steps after applying C2d symmetry. [...] We then increase the system size to 8 x 8, while keeping our ansatz parameters fixed, applying C2d symmetry and while using zero pseudo-temperature. In this phase, the learning rate is fixed to eta = 10^-5. After this step, we train our RNN ansatz until convergence. We repeat the same procedure for system sizes 10 x 10, 12 x 12, 14 x 14 and 16 x 16. We note that for 8 x 8, we add 40000 gradient steps. For 10 x 10, we continue training with 20000 gradient steps. For 12 x 12, we converge using 10000 training steps. For 14 x 14, we continue training with 5000 gradient steps. compute.note: Parameters evaluated: NetKet 3.13.0 Jastrow stores the strictly lower triangle of W, N(N-1)/2 = 196*195/2 = 19110 real (float32) weights, which is also what vmc.py prints as n_params (tree_size_real_nonzero). Samples: 1024 per SR step, 1024 chains of length 1, each sample one sweep of 196 exchange proposals, no discard. Iterations: 10^4 steps (--max_step default). Driver: nkx.driver.VMC_SRt (n_parameters >= n_samples = 1024). After training the energy is estimated from 2^20 samples. stored sigma 0.013 vs sqrt(stored variance 177.484 / 2^20) = 0.013: consistent with the script's 2^20-sample final estimate (--estim_size default). Provenance: the value entered VarBench in 59e621a (2022-09-13, Dian Wu); the linked script was added to varbench/methods in c686621 (2024-07-30) without the value changing, so the script is the authors' later reconstruction of the baseline, not a log of the run (the same holds for the TFIsing RBM rows, scripts/defects.mjs). The 2^20-sample final estimate is corroborated by the stored sigma; batch size and step count are not independently corroborated. No device or time is recorded (the conda env includes CUDA; the README says a GPU is "usually needed for VMC on larger lattices", which is not a statement about these runs).
